sections.COMMENTS:
This Composite Source straddles an area of the southern Apennines between the high Sangro R. and high Volturno R. valleys and the city of Isernia (to the north) and the high Calore R. valley and the city of Benevento (to the south). This source is the northernmost sector of the high-angle, NE-dipping, large normal fault system of the southern Apennines.
Historical and instrumental catalogues (Boschi et al., 2000; Gruppo di Lavoro CPTI, 2004; Pondrelli et al., 2006; Guidoboni et al., 2007) show a remarkably dense destructive seismicity within the area. From north to south, these earthquakes are: June 848 A.D. (Mw 6.0, Sannio), 26 July 1805 (Mw 6.6, Molise), 5 June 1688 (Mw 6.7, Sannio), 99 A.D. (Mw 6.3, Circello), the northern and southern sub-events of the 5 December 1456 (Mw 7.0 and 6.6, respectively) catastrophic, multiple earthquake, 21 August 1962 (Mw 6.2, Irpinia), 14 March 1702 (Mw 6.3, Sannio-Irpinia), and 29 November 1732 (Mw 6.6, Irpinia). Virtually all of the above earthquakes hold several complexities, in part still to be ascertained, concerning the damage scenario, the faulting mechanism, sometimes their very location.
Regarding the 1456 seismic crisis, studied elsewhere in this Database, the reader can refer to Guidoboni and Comastri (2005), and Fracassi and Valensise (2007), and rererences therein.
This Source lies at the backbone of the whole NW-SE striking extensional axis of the southern Apennines, at the passage between the SW-dipping (in Abruzzo) and NE-dipping (in Molise) large normal fault systems from the central to the southern Apennines. This source includes the 25+ km long faults thought to be responsible for the 1805 (to the north) and the 1688 (to the south) earthquakes.
Three segments of this Source have been recognised based on their seismogenic potential. For an in-depth analysis of seismogenesis in this region, the reader can refer to the Individual Sources in this Database.
The strike of this Source was based on that of the mapped structures. The dip was based on geological data and geometrical considerations. The rake represents pure extension, based on geological observations. The minimum and maximum depth were based on geological and seismological data. The slip rate was inferred from geological observations in adjacent structures that share the same tectonic environment with this Source.
